indications.name: Bariatric surgery in adults aged 18 years or older

criteria.text: Uses one of the proven bariatric procedures listed in the coverage rationale
any_of: Biliopancreatic diversion or biliopancreatic diversion with duodenal switch
Gastric bypass, including robotic-assisted gastric bypass
Adjustable gastric banding by open or laparoscopic approach, for individuals ≥ 18 years of age
Sleeve gastrectomy (vertical sleeve gastrectomy)

criteria.text: Body mass index threshold, with lower thresholds for individuals of Asian descent
any_of: BMI ≥ 40 kg/m², or ≥ 35 kg/m² in individuals of Asian descent
BMI 35 to 39.9 kg/m², or 32.5 to 37.4 kg/m² in individuals of Asian descent, with one or more listed comorbidities

criteria.text: For BMI 35 to 39.9 kg/m² (32.5 to 37.4 kg/m² in Asian descent), one or more of these comorbidities
any_of: Insulin resistance or type 2 diabetes

Cardiovascular disease such as history of stroke or myocardial infarction, poorly controlled hypertension despite pharmacotherapy (systolic above 140 mm Hg or diastolic 90 mm Hg or greater), coronary artery disease, or hyperlipidemia
History of cardiomyopathy
Obstructive sleep apnea confirmed on polysomnography with an Apnea-Hypopnea Index or Respiratory Disturbance Index ≥ 30
Evidence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri)

criteria.text: Presurgical preparation by one of two routes
any_of: Both a preoperative evaluation with a detailed weight history and dietary and physical activity patterns, and a psychosocial-behavioral evaluation by a professional in a behavioral health discipline that screens for risk factors or potential postoperative challenges
Participation in a multidisciplinary surgical preparatory regimen

indications.name: Bariatric surgery in adolescents aged 12 to 17 years

criteria.text: Uses one of the proven bariatric procedures listed in the coverage rationale
any_of: Biliopancreatic diversion or biliopancreatic diversion with duodenal switch
Gastric bypass, including robotic-assisted gastric bypass
Adjustable gastric banding by open or laparoscopic approach, for individuals ≥ 18 years of age
Sleeve gastrectomy (vertical sleeve gastrectomy)
Class III obesity
Class II obesity with one or more listed comorbidities

criteria.text: For Class II obesity, one or more of these comorbidities
any_of: Insulin resistance or type 2 diabetes
Poorly controlled hypertension despite pharmacotherapy (systolic above 140 mm Hg or diastolic 90 mm Hg or greater)
Hyperlipidemia
Obstructive sleep apnea confirmed on polysomnography with an Apnea-Hypopnea Index or Respiratory Disturbance Index ≥ 30
Evidence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri)

criteria.text: Evaluation at or in consultation with a multidisciplinary center focused on the surgical treatment of severe childhood obesity
Initial BMI ≥ 50 kg/m² before the first-stage bariatric procedure
Second stage occurs within 2 years after the primary bariatric surgery procedure
Individual has been adherent to nutrition and exercise
Individual meets the medical necessity criteria above at the time of the second-stage procedure
Uses one of the proven bariatric procedures listed in the coverage rationale
any_of: Biliopancreatic diversion or biliopancreatic diversion with duodenal switch
Gastric bypass, including robotic-assisted gastric bypass
Adjustable gastric banding by open or laparoscopic approach, for individuals ≥ 18 years of age
Sleeve gastrectomy (vertical sleeve gastrectomy)

criteria.text: Technical failure or major complication from the initial procedure, such as one of these
any_of: Bowel perforation, including adjustable gastric band erosion
Adjustable gastric band migration (slippage) that cannot be corrected with manipulation or adjustment
Leak
Obstruction confirmed by imaging studies
Staple-line failure
Mechanical adjustable gastric band failure

Uncontrollable reflux related to sleeve gastrectomy after failed maximum nonpharmacological and pharmacological management (such as at least 1 month of double-dose proton pump inhibitor, H2 blocker, or sucralfate), with severe esophagitis grade C or D confirmed by endoscopy

indications.name: Removal of an adjustable gastric band

criteria.text: Removal of the adjustable gastric band and all related components does not result in a revisional surgery

exclusions: Revisional bariatric surgery for any indication other than those listed as proven
Bariatric surgery as the primary treatment for any condition other than obesity
Gastric electrical stimulation with an implantable gastric stimulator
Laparoscopic greater curvature plication, also known as total gastric vertical plication
Mini-gastric bypass, laparoscopic mini-gastric bypass, or one-anastomosis gastric bypass
Single-anastomosis duodenal switch, also known as duodenal switch with single anastomosis or stomach intestinal pylorus-sparing surgery

Transoral endoscopic surgery, including endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (including OverStitch), gastrointestinal liners, intragastric balloon, transoral outlet reduction (TORe), and the TransPyloric Shuttle device
documentation_requirements: Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage
For revision after band slippage, records showing that manipulation or adjustment to correct the slippage was attempted
Documentation of participation in a multidisciplinary preoperative program
site_of_care: Adolescent evaluation at or in consultation with a multidisciplinary center for surgical treatment of severe childhood obesity, which may include centers accredited by the Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program or with similar programmatic components
